title: Tenant-aware report sinks, adaptive routing, and ad-hoc export downloads for compliance evidence
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem: Customers need both scheduled and ad-hoc copies of compliance evidence (PDF/CSV bundles, manifest, checksums) routed to destinations that respect residency, retention, and encryption requirements. Current scheduled export feature is region-blind and limited to single S3-like sinks; ad-hoc downloads are manual and lack signed provenance.

Goal: Build a flexible 'report sinks' layer that can deliver atomic evidence bundles to multiple sink types (S3, SFTP, secure email, tenant S3 with residency tags, signed Drive bundles for managed customers) with adaptive routing rules based on tenant residency, retention locking, and SLA tier. Expose ad-hoc download API for tenants to request on-demand snapshots and provide dashboard and audit trace for each delivery.

Scope and decisions:
- Support sink types: S3 (aws/gcp/azure), SFTP, HTTPS POST webhook, pre-signed secure download (tenant-facing), and encrypted email for managed customers.
- Adaptive routing policies: region-affinity (residency), cost-priority, and SLA-tier fallback (e.g., if primary sink unavailable, route to crypto-signed archival sink in a pre-authorized region).
- Evidence format: signed tar.gz containing CSV(s) + PDF render of the report + JSON manifest with SHA256 checksums and a signed provenance file (JWS) tied to the runtime and snapshot ID.
- Retention: honor tenant-configured retention windows; implement retention locking for legal holds. Deleted-by-tenant vs. retention-locked semantics must be distinct.
- Observability: per-job audit trail (enqueue, snapshot start/end, encryption, upload attempts, final status) surfaced in Console with retry and error categories.
- Security: server-side encryption with customer KMS optional; bundle signing via platform signing key and optional customer-supplied public key verification.
- Performance: snapshot generation must be consistent with existing SLOs; heavy tenants should use reserved capacity for export generation (surge protection).

Out of scope for initial delivery: UI for long-term retention policy editing (will reuse existing retention settings), multi-tenant bundle coalescing across customers.

Acceptance criteria: see acceptance_criteria field.
acceptance_criteria: Admins can add and configure multiple sink endpoints per tenant (S3, SFTP, webhook, email, presigned).
Scheduling UI and API can register recurring exports with per-export routing policy that enforces residency constraints.
On-demand export API returns a signed bundle download URL (time-limited) when requested by an authorized tenant principal.
Every exported bundle includes a JSON manifest with SHA256 checksums and a platform JWS provenance file; checksums verified post-upload in CI for S3 targets.
Retention locking prevents auto-deletion of export bundles until legal hold is cleared; Console surfaces lock status and rationale.
Delivery attempts are retried with exponential backoff; failures recorded with actionable error categories (auth, network, sink-unavailable, storage-quota).
Console shows end-to-end job timeline and per-tenant export metrics (success rate, avg latency, bytes transferred).
Security review completed and KMS integration validated for at least AWS and GCP.
E2E tests exercising primary sink failure -> adaptive routing fallback to archival sink pass in CI.
